# Fit Reports → Content Plan

**Date:** 2026-07-25
**Data:** `src/data/fit-reports.json` (generated by `scripts/compute-fit-reports.ts`)
**Numbers doc:** [FIT_REPORT_SUMMARY.md](FIT_REPORT_SUMMARY.md)

Every number in this plan is copied from the run of 2026-07-25 — 195 recipes × 9
devices = 1,755 computed verdicts. Re-run the generator before publishing; if a
number here disagrees with the JSON, the JSON is right.

---

## 0. Why this is worth building

Every competitor can tell you what a Helix preset sounds like. Nobody can tell
you **whether it will load on your box**, because that answer needs structured
per-block recipe data and per-device capacity rules in the same place. We have
both. A fit report is a computed answer to the single most common pre-purchase
and pre-gig question in this category — *will my thing run this?* — and it
exists for all 195 recipes the moment the script runs.

It is also the rare page that gets *more* defensible as the library grows,
because the interesting part is not the count, it's the per-recipe reason string.

---

## 1. Flagship page — "Will your HX Stomp run these tones?"

**URL:** `/hx-stomp-fit`
**Title tag:** `Will an HX Stomp run these tones? We checked all 195.`
**H1:** Will your HX Stomp run these tones?

### The headline claim

> **Yes — every one of them. 41 need a compromise first, and we'll tell you
> exactly which one.**

That's the honest form of the finding. Not "195 presets!" — the count is the
*evidence*, not the boast. (House rule: no count-flexing eyebrows. The number
appears inside the claim because the claim is a measurement, never as a
standalone "195 recipes" badge.)

The runner-up claim, which is the one that will actually get quoted:

> An HX Stomp has eight blocks. Our chains average seven. The gap is almost
> never the amp — it's the three overdrives we park in the chain so you can
> stomp between them.

### Section outline, with the real numbers

**§1 — The answer, up top.** (Top-third placement matters: 44–55% of cited
passages come from the first third of a page — see AI_SEARCH_PLAYBOOK §10.)

| | HX Stomp |
| --- | --- |
| Loads as written, with room to spare | **154** of 195 |
| Loads, but only just | **41** |
| Won't load without losing something real | **0** |

**§2 — What "only just" means.** Break the 41 down, because the two halves are
different problems:

- **26** fill all eight blocks exactly. They play fine; you cannot add a looper,
  a boost or a second delay without taking something out.
- **15** are over the cap as written and need one specific removal. In 13 of
  those the removal is a *bypassed alternate* — a second or third overdrive
  parked in the chain — so nothing you actually hear changes.
- **2** are over on estimated DSP as well as block count, both because of a
  dual-mic cab.

**§3 — Why our chains run long.** The honest, specific bit:

- 83 of 195 recipes carry at least one bypassed alternate drive.
- 14 of 195 Helix chains are longer than eight blocks. Strip the bypassed
  alternates and only **1** recipe still needs nine active blocks.
- Active-block distribution: 4 blocks ×2 · 5 ×24 · 6 ×114 · 7 ×45 · 8 ×9 · 9 ×1.
- 58 of 195 use a dual-mic cab, which costs roughly what two effects cost.

**§4 — The Stomp vs the Stomp XL.** A genuinely useful, genuinely surprising
result: **all 195 verdicts are identical.** Same DSP, same eight blocks. The XL
buys footswitches and a fourth snapshot, not headroom. Exactly **2** recipes
want more switchable alternates than the Stomp's three switches. If you're
buying for capacity, that upgrade is not the one.

**§5 — And if you have something else.** Table linking to the sibling pages:

| Device | Loads as written | Only just | Won't load | Verdict withheld |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Helix Floor / LT / Rack | 195 | 0 | 0 | — |
| HX Stomp | 154 | 41 | 0 | — |
| HX Stomp XL | 154 | 41 | 0 | — |
| POD Go | 91 | 102 | **2** | — |
| Quad Cortex | 195 | 0 | 0 | — |
| Fractal FM3 | 190 | 5 | 0 | — |
| Fractal FM9 | 195 | 0 | 0 | — |
| Boss Katana Gen 3 | 195 | 0 | 0 | — |
| Kemper Profiler | — | — | — | **195** |

**§6 — Where we refuse to answer.** This section is a trust asset, not an
apology. Kemper gets no verdict on any of the 195, because the amp is a profile
you source yourself and our translations name a Rig Exchange *search*, not a
rig. We publish the effect-slot arithmetic (which is computable — every one of
our Kemper chains fits an MK1's 4 pre + 4 post layout) and stop there. Same
section covers: our DSP figures are role-average estimates, not Line 6's
per-model numbers (`src/lib/helix/dsp-costs.ts` has the better data and the
generator has a TODO to switch); the Katana translations were already trimmed
before we measured them.

**§7 — The full table.** All 195, sortable, filterable by verdict and genre,
each row linking to its recipe page. Verdict + one-line reason inline.

### Sibling pages (same generator, different slice)

- `/pod-go-fit` — the interesting one. **91 fit, 102 tight, 2 don't.** POD Go's
  four free block positions are the tightest real constraint in the whole
  dataset. Headline: *"Two of the 195 need a block POD Go doesn't have."*
- `/katana-fit` — needs the fidelity framing or it's a lie by omission: all 195
  fit, and all 195 Katana translations already leave something out (the
  compressor in 185, the EQ in 141). Headline: *"All 195 fit a Katana. Here's
  what we left out to get there."*
- `/fm3-fit` — 190 / 5 / 0; the 5 are CPU, not grid.
- `/kemper-fit` — the refusal page. "We won't guess which profile you own."

## 2. Fit badges on recipe pages

### Where

Directly under the platform-translation tabs on `/recipes/[slug]`, above the
block table. It answers the question the reader has *before* they read the
settings, and it sits in the page's top third.

### The component

A row of device chips. Default state shows the reader's saved device (localStorage
`fk.device`) expanded, the rest collapsed behind "other devices".

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  WILL IT RUN?                                                │
│                                                              │
│  ● HX Stomp        Tight — one alternate comes out           │
│  ● POD Go          Tight — pick one of the three drives      │
│  ● Katana Gen 3    Fits — 3 of 5 slots                       │
│  ○ Kemper          We don't guess (profile-based)            │
│                                                              │
│  [ Helix Floor · Quad Cortex · FM3 · FM9 ▾ ]                 │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Visual language

Four states, no traffic-light green/amber/red (it reads as pass/fail and three
of the four states are perfectly good outcomes):

| Verdict | Dot | Label | Tone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fits` | filled amber | **Fits** | flat, unexcited |
| `tight` | half-filled amber | **Tight** | matter-of-fact |
| `no` | hollow ink outline | **Needs a cut** | never "fails", never "can't" |
| `not_applicable` | hollow, dashed | **We don't guess** | proud, not apologetic |

Use raw `paper`/`ink`/`amber` CSS vars — `bg-surface`/`text-muted` leak the dark
global theme outside `.post-body`.

Expanding a chip reveals the full `reason` string plus, when present, the
`cuts` list rendered as an ordered "if you have to lose something" list, and
`caveats` as a footnote.

### Microcopy rules

1. **Never say "can't".** Say what it costs. "Needs a cut" + the specific cut.
2. **Name the block, not the category.** "Drop the Heir Apparent", not "drop a
   drive block".
3. **Say what you keep.** Every `no` and every `tight` ends with what survives.
4. **Label estimates.** Any DSP number renders as "est. 90%" with a tooltip
   pointing at the method section.
5. **Never imply we tested it.** These are computed from block counts and
   published specs. The badge tooltip says "Computed from the chain, not
   measured on hardware" — consistent with the /experiment honest-authorship
   rules.

## 3. `/which-modeler` — song-driven device recommendation

A scorecard funnel, not a personality quiz. The input is the songs the player
actually needs to cover; the output is a device recommendation with the
arithmetic shown.

### Flow

**Step 1 — Pick your songs.** Search/multi-select over the 195 recipes,
prefilled with the reader's most-viewed. Minimum 3, recommended 8–12 (a set).

**Step 2 — Two constraints.**
- Budget band: under $500 / $500–1,000 / $1,000+ / doesn't matter
- How you play: bedroom + headphones / church or bar stage / recording / all three

**Step 3 — Results.** Per device: how many of *your* songs land in each bucket,
then a recommendation.

### Scoring logic (deterministic, no ML, no vibes)

```
for each device D:
  fits[D]   = count(selected songs where verdict == "fits")
  tight[D]  = count(... == "tight")
  no[D]     = count(... == "no")
  score[D]  = fits[D] * 1.0 + tight[D] * 0.6 + no[D] * 0.0
  penalty   = 0.15 * count(songs where translation_fidelity == "reduced")
  final[D]  = (score[D] / selected.length) - penalty
```

- Devices with any `no` are never recommended first, however high the score.
- `not_applicable` (Kemper) is excluded from ranking and shown separately with
  the refusal copy — never silently dropped, or we look like we forgot Kemper.
- The budget band filters the candidate set *before* ranking, so a POD Go can
  win an under-$500 answer that a Helix Floor would otherwise take.
- The fidelity penalty is what stops the Katana winning everything: it fits all
  195, but 195 of those verdicts rest on a trimmed chain.

### Result copy pattern

> **For your 9 songs: HX Stomp.**
> 7 load as written. 2 are tight — *Comfortably Numb* fills all eight blocks
> once you drop the bypassed Heir Apparent, and *Walk* needs the same treatment.
> None of the nine need a cut you'd hear.
>
> **Also worth knowing:** a POD Go covers 6 of the 9 outright, and 3 would cost
> you the compressor. A Katana runs all 9 — but our Katana chains already leave
> the compressor out on 8 of them, so it's a different tone, not a smaller one.

That last paragraph is the whole product in miniature: we recommend against our
own simplest answer because the data says the comparison isn't apples to apples.

### Lead capture

Email the result as a PDF "device shortlist for your set" — a scorecard funnel
converting at the 30–50% band this format normally hits. No gate on the on-page
result; the PDF is the upgrade.

## 4. SEO / AEO approach

Per `docs/AI_SEARCH_PLAYBOOK.md`: AEO *is* SEO, visible on-page content is the
retrieval lever, and JSON-LD is belt-and-braces for classic rich results — not
an AI-citation play. No llms.txt, no chunking hacks, no schema stuffing.

### What actually does the work

1. **The reason strings are the retrievable unit.** Each one is a complete,
   self-contained answer to a sub-query ("does Comfortably Numb fit on an HX
   Stomp"). AI fan-out matches sub-queries beyond the top 20 — one narrow,
   completely-answered question per row is structurally correct.
2. **Titles phrased as the sub-query.** `Will an HX Stomp run [song]?` on the
   recipe page's fit section heading; `Will your HX Stomp run these tones?` on
   the hub.
3. **Answer in the top third.** The fit table is the first content block on the
   flagship page; the fit badges sit above the settings table on recipe pages.
4. **Non-Commodity Gate.** These pages pass on criterion 1 without argument:
   the per-recipe verdict does not exist in any competitor's top-5 SERP, because
   nobody else has the structured chain data to compute it.
5. **IndexNow on publish** (already shipped, CI post-deploy) + Bing Webmaster
   sitemap check, since Bing retrievability is the ChatGPT lever.

### JSON-LD (keep it boring)

- Flagship page: `Article` + `BreadcrumbList`. Optionally one `FAQPage` for the
  three real questions the page answers ("Will an HX Stomp run these?", "Is the
  XL any bigger?", "Why won't you answer for Kemper?"). Belt-and-braces only.
- Recipe pages: **no new schema type for fit.** There is no `schema.org`
  vocabulary for "does this preset fit this device", and inventing
  `additionalProperty` soup to fake one is exactly the hack the playbook rules
  out. The visible badge is the retrievable artefact.
- `/which-modeler`: no `Quiz`/`HowTo` markup. Google deprecated HowTo rich
  results for most sites in 2023 and the quiz's value is the on-page answer.
- Do publish `src/data/fit-reports.json` at a stable URL (`/data/fit-reports.json`)
  and link it from the method section. Machine-readable primary data, openly
  linked, is the credibility move — and it's consistent with the MCP/agent
  surface we already run.

### Internal linking

Recipe page fit badge → device hub (`/hx-stomp-fit`) → filtered recipe list →
individual recipes. Device hubs cross-link to each other through the §5
comparison table. `/which-modeler` links out to all nine hubs.

## 5. Exact copy for three fit verdicts

These are the tone reference. Honest, specific, and they always end with what
survives. All three are real verdicts from the current run, lightly edited for
prose rhythm — the generator's raw strings are in the JSON.

### A. `tight` — Pink Floyd, "Comfortably Numb" (solo) on an HX Stomp

> **Tight.** Nine blocks against the Stomp's eight. The block that goes is the
> Heir Apparent — it's bypassed in the recipe anyway, sitting there as an
> alternate fuzz for you to stomp. Delete it and you're at eight of eight, est.
> 90% DSP. Nothing you actually hear changes; what you give up is the option to
> switch fuzzes mid-song. Keep the Triangle Fuzz, the compressor, the tape
> delay and the plate — that's the solo.

### B. `no` — John Mayer, "Slow Dancing in a Burning Room" on a POD Go

> **Needs a cut.** POD Go gives you four free block positions and this chain
> wants six: compressor, Minotaur, Scream 808, Heir Apparent, Transistor Tape
> and Dynamic Plate. The Heir Apparent is a bypassed alternate, so it comes out
> for free — you're still one over. The cheapest real cut is the Deluxe Comp:
> the amp is doing a lot of the compressing already, and this tone lives on the
> delay and the plate far more than on 2 dB of squeeze. Keep both drives, the
> tape and the reverb. One more thing: POD Go's Cab/IR slot is one cab and one
> mic, so the recipe's dual-mic blend collapses to a single mic. You lose the
> blend, not the character.

### C. `tight` (second-amp case) — System of a Down, "Spiders" on an HX Stomp

> **Tight.** Only six blocks, so this looks easy — but two of them are amps,
> and no single-DSP box runs two amp models at once. We put est. 102% DSP on
> the chain as written. The second Brit 2203 is bypassed in the recipe; it's an
> alternate voicing, not part of the sound. Drop it and you're at five blocks
> and est. 70% DSP, with headroom for a boost or a second delay. On a Stomp the
> move is to keep one amp and use the Drive block's alternate setting for the
> harder voice: you lose the blend, you keep the character.

**Why these three:** A is the common case (an alternate comes out, nothing is
lost). B is the genuinely hard case, and shows us recommending against a block
*we chose to put in the recipe*. C is the counter-intuitive one — a six-block
chain that doesn't fit — and it's the sentence the brief asked for, earned by
the data rather than pasted in.

## 6. Build order

1. **Ship the data.** `scripts/compute-fit-reports.ts` is done and run; wire it
   into the weekly audit cron so verdicts can't go stale against the recipes.
2. **Fit badges on recipe pages.** Highest value per hour — 195 pages get a new
   differentiated section from one component. Render via `OverlayPortal` if the
   expanded state becomes a drawer.
3. **`/hx-stomp-fit`.** One page, the strongest claim, the clearest audience
   (SEO target segment is worship guitarists on Helix/HX Stomp — this is
   squarely on-target, see TARGET_SEGMENT_AND_SEO_STRATEGY.md).
4. **`/pod-go-fit` and `/katana-fit`.** The two with the most interesting data.
5. **`/which-modeler`.** Most build effort, needs the hubs to link into first.

## 7. Before any of this ships

- Switch the generator to `src/lib/helix/dsp-costs.ts` (TODO at the top of the
  script). Publishing role-average DSP estimates on a page whose whole value is
  precision is a bad trade when the per-model table already exists in the repo.
- Fix the 5 miscategorised blocks the generator flagged (a Compressor and a
  Noise Gate filed under the Katana's Booster slot, a Cry Baby filed under
  Fractal's Drive). They're currently corrected by name at read time; the data
  should just be right.
- Decide whether "the Katana translation drops the compressor on 185 of 195" is
  a data bug or a standard. `RECIPE_STANDARD.md` § mirror exemptions says it's
  by design for Gen 1/2 — but the Gen 3 Mod/FX pool has a Comp. If the standard
  is out of date, the `/katana-fit` page is the thing that will expose it.
